key_insight: The paper replaces kinetic energy in optimal transport with Barron energy, turning transport planning into a measure of neural-network complexity for generative modeling.
engineering_relevance: It offers a principled way to compare and design generative samplers by quantifying how efficiently a neural model can transport a simple reference distribution to a target one.
method: Formulate optimal transport with Benamou–Brenier dynamics but swap the usual $L^2$ kinetic cost for Barron norm cost.
Interpret each time step of a transport flow as a neural hidden layer approximating instantaneous velocity.
Use the resulting geometry to analyze generative models and derive lower bounds for score approximation in diffusion models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and lower-bound results, including super-polynomial score approximation lower bounds for data produced by neural-network pushforwards of a Gaussian.
watch_item: The framework is theoretically elegant but may be difficult to compute or optimize directly in high-dimensional practical generative systems.
paper_title: Barron Optimal Transport I: Generative Modeling
